## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Devasadda Sutta* ("The Cry of the Gods", Iti 82; PTS It 75) is located in the third section (Tikanipāta) of the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. The sutta outlines three occasions on which celestial beings (*devas*) utter cries of joy and acclaim regarding the spiritual conduct and achievements of human beings (*tayo devesu devasaddā niccharanti*) [SuttaCentral; Windisch 1889]. Ernst Windisch's 1889 edition of the Pali text includes the prose conclusion of the discourse describing the third cry, raised when a noble disciple realizes awakening through higher knowledge and overcomes worldly struggles (*eso ariyasāvako vijitasaṅgāmo*), which is then followed by a summary verse (*disvā vijitasaṅgāmaṃ*) [Windisch 1889].
According to SuttaCentral, a resembling parallel exists in Chinese translation at T 765.139 [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus additionally aligns sections of the sutta with the Chinese *Dà jiāngù póluómén yuánqǐ jīng* (大堅固婆羅門緣起經, T 8) [DharmaNexus]. In Pali literature, DharmaNexus records 209 matching passages across 23 canonical texts; the largest shares of text reuse occur with the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (particularly AN 5 with 43 matches, AN 10, AN 7, and AN 3), the *Jhānavibhaṅga* of the *Vibhaṅga* (Vb 12), the *Ekuttarikanaya* of the *Parivāra* (Pvr 7), and Dīgha Nikāya discourses such as the *Āṭānāṭiya Sutta* (DN 32) and *Mahāpadāna Sutta* (DN 14), alongside closely adjacent suttas in the *Itivuttaka* itself (Iti 81 and Iti 87) [DharmaNexus].
